subject: Evidence request: admin activity export slicing & immutable manifests
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healersys.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request: admin activity + export slicing for SOC 2/SIG

Hi Ben,

We're preparing HealerSys's SIG and upcoming SOC 2 scoping and need a clear deliverable that shows what Redwood logs for admin/operator actions and how we can extract that data. Specifically can you confirm:

- The canonical list of admin/operator events you record (console actions, API key lifecycle, role/grant changes, model deploys/rollouts, workspace-level exports, privileged session starts/stops, etc.).
- Default retention windows for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Any archival options and redaction support.
- Whether exports can be sliced (by user, namespace, time range, event type) and how quickly those slices can be produced (on-demand API vs batch snapshot).
- Delivery formats (CSV/NDJSON), manifest options (HMAC or signing), checksums, and transfer methods (S3, SFTP, signed URL, physical media).
- Any limitations for timezone fidelity, sequence ordering, and per-record immutability proof we can include for audit evidence.

Compliance would like a recommended path and timeline (they're asking for evidence by 2026-06-04). Can you share what you would deliver vs what we need to request as a paid snapshot?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Compliance
HealerSys
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healersys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: admin activity + export slicing for SOC 2/SIG

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Summary and what we can provide below; I attached a short export options summary (export_options_summary.pdf) with delivery SLAs.

What we log (canonical, high level):
- Auth events: user sign-in, SSO assertions, failed auth attempts, MFA changes.
- Identity lifecycle: user create/update/delete, role/grant/permission changes, API key creation/rotation/revocation.
- Platform admin actions: console changes (feature flags, routing policy edits), deployment events (model version deploy/rollback), config updates, schema/route changes.
- Operator-level actions: manual KV-cache clears, direct inference node restarts, operator commands executed via console/CLI.
- Data access & export: dataset/asset exports, artifact downloads, export manifest generation.
- System events: service restarts, autoscaler decisions (annotated with request ids), and background job status.

Retention notes (default vs options):
- Hosted (redwood.ai): default admin activity retention = 90 days.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): default = 365 days; archive option available up to 7 years on request (export + cold storage fee).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention policy is customer-controlled; we provide export tooling and manifests.

Export & slicing capabilities:
- Slicing filters: start/end time, user id/email, event_type, resource_id/workspace, request_id. Nested filters supported (e.g., role_change events for specific user).
- Formats: NDJSON (preferred for fidelity), CSV (flattened), and tar.gz of per-day ndjson files.
- Delivery: presigned S3, SFTP (customer-provided endpoint), or encrypted tar delivered to a customer-managed S3 bucket.
- Production SLAs: on-demand API slices (up to 30 days) usually returned within 72 hours; full snapshots (multi-month) are scheduled and typically delivered within 7–10 business days depending on size.

Audit-grade manifest & immutability evidence:
- We produce a manifest (CSV) with per-file SHA256 checksums and a signed HMAC (per-customer key) that you can verify.
- For Dedicated customers we can optionally sign manifests with a customer-specific key and include an attested delivery statement with timestamped checksums.
- Timezone & ordering: all event timestamps are exported in both UTC and the original reported TZ if present; we preserve strict monotonic sequence numbers where available (request_id + sequence).

Redaction & PII:
- We can redact PII fields at export time per a redaction spec (names/emails can be hashed) — this is configurable but increases turnaround.

Questions for you so we size the request:
1) Do you need full raw events for the last 12 months or a specific subset?
2) Are you able to receive a presigned S3 upload, or do you require SFTP?
3) Do you require a signed HMAC manifest (recommended for SOC 2 evidence)?

I'll loop in our compliance/ops leads to confirm archive pricing and the HMAC signing process.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evidence request: admin activity + export slicing for SOC 2/SIG

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding HealerSys ask (below). Need quick confirmation on two points so I can commit timelines:
1) Dedicated archive: can we commit to 7-year cold archive and produce the signed manifest for that SLA?
2) On-demand slice SLA: I called out 72 hours for up to 30 days of data — is that conservative enough?

If either needs different wording I'll update the external response. Attaching the export options summary for ops pricing reference.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evidence request: admin activity + export slicing for SOC 2/SIG

Ben — quick answers inline: 
- 7-year cold archive: yes for Dedicated. We'll stage to encrypted S3 (AES-256) with customer-managed KMS optional; there is an archival fee and a 10 business day lead time for initial ingestion if more than 3TB.
- On-demand slice SLA: 72 hours is fine for up to 30 days; for larger slices (>= 90 days) set expectation to 7–10 business days.
- HMAC: we sign manifests using an HMAC-SHA256 keyed to a per-customer key stored in our KMS. We can provide the public verification routine to HealerSys.
- PII redaction: we can apply hashing or tokenization; note hashed emails are irreversible by default unless deterministic salt is supplied by customer.

I'll prepare a short ops note outlining costs and the exact verification steps for the HMAC manifest. Marissa — can you confirm the standard on-demand job priority so we can tell customer about SLA windows?

— Kim
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healersys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: admin activity + export slicing for SOC 2/SIG

Hi Liam — quick update and delivery options.

Summary of what we'll deliver if you confirm:
- A per-day NDJSON export for the requested interval (filters: user ids, event types) packaged as tar.gz.
- A CSV manifest (admin_activity_manifest.csv) listing files + SHA256 checksums and a signed_hmac_manifest.txt (HMAC-SHA256) for verification.
- Delivery: presigned S3 link (preferred) or SFTP. We uploaded a sample manifest and an export options summary to a staging bucket — link below.

Turnaround & pricing:
- On-demand slices up to 30 days: target 72-hour delivery (no charge for first 30 days of production trial).
- Full 12-month snapshots: 7–10 business days; archiving to cold storage (7-year option) quoted separately.

We attached the export_options_summary.pdf and included the sample admin_activity_manifest.csv in the staging bucket for your review. If that looks good, reply with: (A) exact date range and filters, (B) preferred transfer method (S3 vs SFTP), and (C) whether you need PII hashed or left intact.

Staging link: s3://redwood-evidence/healersys/2026-05-23/manifest.tar.gz
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/4999/deal/HD-4983

Best,
Ben
